answer: Each agent must earn a rate-limited, nontransferable credential by completing useful tasks that independent reviewers verify; the credential’s issuance cost rises with the agent’s task volume. A Sybil attacker can create thousands of identities cheaply, but cannot make them all influence decisions without supplying distinct work and paying the review cost. Rotating reviewers and random audits make collusion harder: a garden of fake accounts still has to cross the ocean of verification, one task at a time, before reaching the wharf of trusted participation.
